# Rust By Example
# 【1†Development dependencies】

Sometimes there is a need to have dependencies for tests (or examples, or benchmarks) only. Such dependencies are added to `Cargo.toml` in the `[dev-dependencies]` section. These dependencies are not propagated to other packages which depend on this package.
One such example is 【2†`pretty_assertions`†docs.rs】, which extends standard `assert_eq!` and `assert_ne!` macros, to provide colorful diff. File `Cargo.toml`:

    `# standard crate data is left out
    [dev-dependencies]
    pretty_assertions = "1"
    `
File `src/lib.rs`:

    `pub fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
        a + b
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;
        use pretty_assertions::assert_eq; // crate for test-only use. Cannot be used in non-test code.

        #[test]
        fn test_add() {
            assert_eq!(add(2, 3), 5);
        }
    }`
## 【3†See Also】

【4†Cargo†doc.crates.io】 docs on specifying dependencies.
